prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1276; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant reports neck pain with whiplash symptoms and is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is listed as a named driver and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the lane change and the contact between the two vehicles as the claimant described. Requested photos from the scene and a copy of the police report.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the vehicle inspection show damage consistent with the reported impact. No earlier damage to either vehicle has come to light in the records reviewed so far.

Entry 5: Witness statement received and it matches the account given by both drivers. The witness described the sideswipe in the same sequence and location.

Entry 6: The claimant's initial statement was given through counsel. Follow-up questions added a few minor details about the moments before and after impact, but the core account has not changed.

Entry 7: Medical records reviewed. The whiplash diagnosis is plausible for this type of collision, and no prior treatment to the neck or upper back appears in the records or in the prior claims search.

Entry 8: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested updated treatment notes and a timeline of visits from the provider to better understand the course of care.

Entry 9: Still unclear from the statements and photos exactly where the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the moment of impact. Asked counsel to clarify the seating position in writing.

Entry 10: Reserve reviewed and file remains open pending the updated treatment notes and the clarification on seating position. No coverage issues identified at this time.
